site.name: Pawanpreet Singh
site.intro: I build small, native Apple apps. The kind that open fast, keep your data on your own device, and then get out of the way.
bio: I'm an iOS engineer on the founding team at Ultrahuman. Before that: Zomato, LimeTray, Zolo.
Apple gave me a WWDC Student Scholarship in 2016 and I've written Swift most days since. All of it was built after hours, by one person, with no team and no funding.
One idea runs through all of it. Build native. Compute on the device. Send nothing home.

principles.d: SwiftUI and UIKit, Metal where it earns its keep, and Apple Watch, widgets, Live Activities and Vision Pro built properly rather than ticked off.
Storage on your device, sync through your own iCloud if you want it. No account to make, nothing to log into, no server holding your history.
When an app makes a claim about your body or your money it shows its working: the sample size, the confidence, and the reasons it might be wrong.

apps.name: Moon
apps.tagline: The real moon, exactly as you see it.
apps.blurb: A photorealistic lunar sphere rendered in Metal and lit at tonight's true phase. Spin it like a globe, drag a timeline to watch it wax and wane through any date, then pull up a glass drawer of precise figures: illumination, moonrise and moonset, distance, altitude and azimuth.
apps.detail: A single on-device astronomy engine built on Meeus' algorithms feeds every surface: iPhone, iPad, Mac, Vision Pro, Apple Watch, widgets and complications. The moon is oriented to your sky rather than to a stock illustration, at your latitude, on your date.
highlights: Metal-rendered sphere with a true terminator
Scrub the timeline to any date

privacy.summary: Zero network access. Every figure is computed on your device.
privacy.location: When-In-Use, used on-device to orient the sky, never transmitted

iap.name: Moon Pro
iap.trial: No trial; a single one-time purchase
iap.free: The moon, the timeline and the facts drawer, in full.
iap.unlocks: The Moon Details widget, and rise, set and special-event alerts.

apps.name: Pomodoro
apps.tagline: Deep focus, one tomato at a time.
apps.blurb: A native focus timer built on the Pomodoro technique: twenty-five minute sprints, breaks you actually take, and a task list light enough to keep using. Streaks and heatmaps make the effort visible without turning it into a game you can lose.
apps.detail: The timer lives everywhere the system allows. Home and Lock Screen widgets, Live Activities with Dynamic Island, a full Apple Watch app with complications, and Siri Shortcuts. You can start a session and steer it without ever opening the app.

privacy.summary: Timers and tasks sync through your own private iCloud. Purchase state and usage analytics go to third-party services.
privacy.storage: Core Data, synced to your private iCloud (CloudKit)
privacy.analytics: Amplitude: product analytics on how the app is used

iap.name: Pomodoro Pro
iap.free: Four completed work sessions a day and five active tasks.
iap.unlocks: Unlimited sessions and tasks, full history, every accent colour, and the Pro widgets.

apps.name: WaterMyPlants
apps.tagline: Never let a plant go thirsty.
apps.blurb: Watering reminders sized to each plant instead of a generic weekly nag. Add a plant, say how much it drinks and how often, and the app remembers the rest.
apps.detail: The oldest app here and the one that reaches furthest back, still supporting iOS 16. Rebuilt around a Liquid Glass redesign with photo-forward cards, an Apple Watch app and a widget. Ships in English and Hindi.
highlights: A schedule per plant, not per app

privacy.summary: Plants and photos live on your device and sync through your own private iCloud.
privacy.storage: Core Data, synced to your private iCloud

apps.name: Enso
apps.tagline: Spend on purpose: Need, Want, Invest.
apps.blurb: An expense tracker organised around intent rather than category. Every expense is a Need, a Want or an Investment, a modern read on 50/30/20, so the log tells you whether you should have bought it and not merely what it was.
apps.detail: Log in any currency and report in one. Receipt OCR runs on the device. There is no bank linking and no account: the only thing that ever leaves your phone is an anonymous request for exchange rates.
highlights: Budgeting by Need, Want and Investment

privacy.summary: No bank linking and no accounts. The only thing sent out is an anonymous exchange-rate lookup.
privacy.storage: SwiftData on-device, with opt-in private iCloud sync

apps.name: Helia
apps.blurb: A vitamin D tracker that estimates what you actually synthesised, from the sun's real angle at your location, your skin type, what you were wearing and how long you stayed out.
apps.detail: The hero is a living sky that follows the weather and the hour. Every figure is presented as an estimate and carries a medical disclaimer, because that is exactly what it is. Your location is rounded to about a kilometre before anything is calculated.
highlights: A sky that tracks weather and time

privacy.summary: Health data is read live and never synced. Your location is coarsened to roughly a kilometre.
privacy.storage: SwiftData on-device, with opt-in private iCloud sync
privacy.location: Coarse location, rounded to ~1 km, used for solar geometry
privacy.health: HealthKit is read live on-device and never uploaded

apps.name: Flux
apps.tagline: Hydration you can feel, one glass at a time.
apps.blurb: Tap a glass and watch a real body of water rise toward the day's goal. An optional coffee-toned second page tracks caffeine beside it and pairs it with your sleep, so you can see what the afternoon flat white actually costs.
apps.detail: Not every drink hydrates equally, so each carries its own hydration factor: coffee, juice and alcohol count for less. Behind it sits a catalogue of roughly 1,880 real menu drinks across about 35 brands.
highlights: An animated wave as the whole interface

privacy.summary: No account, no login, ever. Its privacy manifest declares no tracking and no collected data.
privacy.storage: A single JSON file in the app's own container. No cloud sync.
privacy.health: Optional two-way Apple Health for water and sleep

apps.name: Linen
apps.tagline: A quiet archive for the looks you love.
apps.blurb: Save the fashion images you like, usually screenshots, and Linen trims the app chrome away, reads the caption, pulls the outfit's colours and files each look into a masonry wall and a shelf of linen-bound seasonal volumes.
apps.detail: Built to feel like a case-bound book rather than a utility: bone paper, warm charcoal ink, square corners, hairline rules. Your photographs are the only real colour in the app. All the vision work runs on the device and the original screenshot is discarded once it has been trimmed.
highlights: Colour and caption read on device

privacy.summary: No network calls at all. Images never leave your device unless you export them.
privacy.storage: Images stored on-device in the app group; opt-in iCloud

apps.name: Stack
apps.tagline: Track your stack. Test what works.
apps.blurb: A supplement tracker with an honest experiments layer. Tick off what you took, tap a chip for how you felt, then compare any supplement against an Apple Health metric. Magnesium days against deep sleep, for instance.
apps.detail: The experiments engine is honest by construction. It refuses to show a result below seven matched days, leads with effect size rather than a p-value, flags confounders, states its confidence in plain language, and never implies a correlation is a cause.

privacy.summary: Health data is read live and never persisted or uploaded.
privacy.health: HealthKit is read live on-device and never persisted or uploaded

apps.name: Slate
apps.blurb: A to-do app that separates the day you mean to do something from the day it is actually due. Most task apps collapse the two, and that is the distinction that decides whether your list stays honest.
apps.detail: Areas, projects, and a today view that organises itself. The only permissions it asks for are read-only calendar access and notifications, both optional. No location, no health data, no analytics.

privacy.summary: Two optional permissions, no trackers, and sync that rides on your own iCloud.
privacy.storage: SwiftData in the app group, mirrored to private CloudKit

apps.name: Folio
apps.tagline: A quiet place to write, everywhere.
apps.blurb: Notes with real typographic care. Nine complete themes, each with its own palette, typeface and page decoration, plus rich text, images and Pencil sketches, synced through your own iCloud.
apps.detail: Face ID can lock a single note or the whole app. Everything is stored on device and mirrored to private CloudKit, on by default, because sync that rides on your own iCloud costs nothing and has no business being a paid tier.
highlights: Face ID on a note or the app

privacy.summary: No third-party servers and no trackers. Notes sync through your own iCloud.
privacy.storage: SwiftData on-device with private CloudKit sync

apps.name: Flaps
apps.blurb: Apple Health rendered as a split-flap departure board. Steps, sleep, resting heart rate and exercise clatter into place the way an airport board announces the next departure.
apps.detail: A custom flip engine drives the entire identity, with twenty themes each carrying its own accent. The app is strictly read-only and entirely on device: it takes a snapshot of Health and shows it back to you.

privacy.summary: Read-only and entirely on your device. No accounts, no cloud, no analytics.
privacy.storage: An app-group JSON snapshot on your device

apps.name: Haru
apps.blurb: A routine sequencer. An ordered list of short timed steps that you press play on and then simply follow. Haptics lead, so you can run a morning routine without looking at the screen.
apps.detail: Local first, no account, no feed, and none of the anxiety mechanics habit apps reach for. Nothing is fetched at build time either: the whole thing is a local package with no dependencies.

privacy.summary: No account, no network, no feed.

apps.name: Meridian
apps.tagline: A precision world clock, on a globe that is actually alive.
apps.blurb: A worldtimer built around a live dot globe with a real day and night terminator, projected and rotating rather than drawn once, with weather as ambient context instead of the main event.
apps.detail: Time zones, city search and the solar maths are all computed on the device. Only the weather touches the network, and without it the app degrades to a fully working world clock. Aeroplane mode is a supported configuration, not a failure state.
highlights: Time zones and solar maths offline
Widgets on every one of them

privacy.summary: Every time and every sunrise is computed on your device; your cities and people live in your own private iCloud, and none of it is ever sent to me.
privacy.storage: On-device (SwiftData), synced through your private iCloud database — readable by no one else, including me
thirdparty: Apple Weather (WeatherKit) — receives the coordinates of your saved cities, taken from the app's bundled atlas rather than your device's location, to fetch current conditions
Open-Meteo — receives the same city coordinates as a fallback when Apple Weather has no answer; no account, no key, no identifier
RevenueCat — validates App Store purchases; receives the store receipt and a random anonymous app id, never your name, email or contents
Tally — only if you choose to open a feedback form, the link carries the app version, OS version, device model and locale so reports are actionable; nothing is sent unless you submit the form

iap.name: Meridian Pro
iap.trial: No trial and no subscription; a single one-time purchase
iap.free: The whole instrument — the globe, the sight, the sun bar, golden hour, clock-change warnings — plus three saved cities and three people.
iap.unlocks: Unlimited cities and people, custom places included, and the widgets' sun-arc Detail faces.

apps.name: Threshold
apps.tagline: Zones anchored to your threshold, not to 220 minus your age.
apps.blurb: Heart-rate zone training for Apple Watch and iPhone, built on lactate threshold rather than the borrowed percentage-of-maximum model most zone apps still use.
apps.detail: The incumbent in this category puts custom zone boundaries behind a paywall and derives them from a formula that was never meant to be precise. Threshold inverts both. Accessibility, dark mode and localisation were in scope from the first commit.

privacy.summary: Workouts are read from Apple Health on-device and stay there.
privacy.location: Used during workouts for route and pace

apps.name: Apex
apps.blurb: A Formula 1 companion: live timing with sector splits, championship standings, circuit maps that mark the overtaking zones, tyre stints, and driver and constructor profiles carrying a whole career rather than eleven rounds of one.
apps.detail: Hand-drawn track maps, a reaction-lights game, season history, widgets and an Apple Watch app. An independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Formula 1.

privacy.summary: Fetches published race data. No account, no analytics.
thirdparty: A public Formula 1 results and timing data source

apps.name: Cabin
apps.tagline: A calmer set of car controls.
apps.blurb: Climate, charging, locks and location for an electric car, plus a tyre-pressure watch and a history view. Built because the official app buries the four things you use daily behind everything else.
apps.detail: A personal project rather than a store submission. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Tesla, Inc.
highlights: Climate and charging at a glance
Widgets for the four daily controls

privacy.summary: Talks to the vehicle's own API using your credentials. Nothing is sent anywhere else.

apps.name: Flap Pomodoro
apps.blurb: The Pomodoro technique rendered as a split-flap board, with the minutes physically falling away, plus a Mac menu bar timer, tasks and statistics.
apps.detail: A design study that turned into a real app: the same timer idea as Pomodoro given a completely different physical metaphor, then taken across iPhone, Mac, Apple TV, Vision Pro and Watch.
